title: FastAPI Dependency Injection: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes for FastAPI's Depends system: the mental model, dependency trees, yield setup/teardown, class and global dependencies, and test overrides. Ends with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Depends and the Mental Model
points: Dependency injection: a parameter declared as Depends(callable) is resolved by FastAPI before the handler runs, and the callable's return value is passed in
Any callable works as a dependency (function, async function, class); its own parameters are parsed like path function params (path, query, header, body)
Sync deps run in a threadpool; async deps run on the event loop, so mixing is fine but a blocking call inside async def stalls the loop
Pass the function itself: Depends(get_db) is correct, Depends(get_db()) calls it at import time and injects a fixed value
Example: def common(q: str | None = None, limit: int = 10): return {'q': q, 'limit': limit}; @app.get('/items') def items(p: dict = Depends(common))

chapters.title: Dependency Trees and Caching
points: Sub-dependencies: a dependency can itself declare Depends(...) params, forming a tree that FastAPI resolves bottom-up
Per-request cache: if the same dependency callable appears several times in one tree, it runs once and the result is shared
Depends(dep, use_cache=False) forces a fresh call each time it is declared
Typical chain: get_db -> get_current_user (needs token + db) -> require_admin (needs user); the endpoint only declares require_admin
Annotated alias for reuse: CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]; then def me(user: CurrentUser)

chapters.title: Yield Dependencies: Setup and Teardown
points: A dependency with yield runs code before yield as setup, injects the yielded value, and runs code after yield as teardown once the response is sent
Standard pattern: def get_db(): db = Session(); try: yield db finally: db.close(), where the finally guarantees cleanup even when the handler raises
Teardown order is reverse of setup: the last dependency set up is the first torn down
Exceptions raised in the handler are re-raised at the yield point, so catch them there to rollback; you can't change the response from teardown code (it has already started streaming)
Use one yield per dependency; an async def with yield is an async context manager, and a plain def with yield runs in a threadpool

chapters.title: Class Dependencies and Global Dependencies
points: A class is callable, so Depends(Pagination) calls Pagination(...) and its __init__ params are read as query/path params
Shortcut: Depends() with no argument uses the type annotation as the callable: def f(p: Pagination = Depends())
Class dependency wins when you need typed attribute access (p.skip, p.limit) and editor autocomplete instead of dict keys
Route decorator dependencies: @app.get('/x', dependencies=[Depends(verify_key)]) runs the dep but discards its return value

Router-level: APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(auth)]) covers every route in it; app-level: FastAPI(dependencies=[Depends(auth)]) covers every route; order is app, then router, then route, then parameters

chapters.title: Overriding Dependencies in Tests
points: app.dependency_overrides[original_dep] = fake_dep replaces a dependency for every request; the key is the original function object itself, not a string
Fake keeps the original's parameter shape or declares its own: its params are resolved by FastAPI as usual, so overriding get_current_user with lambda: User(id=1) skips auth entirely
Example: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: test_session; client = TestClient(app); client.get('/items')
Reset after each test: app.dependency_overrides.clear() or a pytest fixture with yield, otherwise overrides leak into later tests
Override the exact function object used in Depends; an Annotated alias still works since it wraps the same function, but an imported copy or wrapper does not match

chapters.title: Dependency Cheat Sheet
points: Declare: param: Annotated[T, Depends(fn)]; pass fn uncalled; use_cache=False disables per-request reuse
Yield dep: setup, yield value, finally teardown; teardown runs in reverse order after the response
Class dep: Depends(Cls) or Depends(); read attributes like p.skip
Scope ladder: route dependencies=[...] < APIRouter(dependencies=[...]) < FastAPI(dependencies=[...]); return values are discarded at these levels
Testing: app.dependency_overrides[orig] = fake; clear() in fixture teardown
